userStories.title: Create trading_events.py with event enums and dataclasses
userStories.description: As a developer, I need strongly-typed trading event definitions so that the event bus and queue can validate payloads.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/trading_events.py
TradingEventType enum has 8 members: TRADE_OPENED, TRADE_CLOSED, TRADE_MODIFIED, POLICY_BLOCKED, RETRAIN_REQUESTED, DEGRADED_MODE_ENTERED, DEGRADED_MODE_EXITED, QUEUE_FAILURE

TradingEvent dataclass has fields: event_id (str), event_type (TradingEventType), timestamp (str), source (str), payload_version (int, default=1), session_id (str), correlation_id (str), payload (dict)

TradeClosedPayload dataclass has at least 18 fields: trade_id, pair, direction, entry_price, exit_price, realized_pl, pnl_pips, trade_won, exit_reason, duration_minutes, confidence, regime, agent_reasons, model, analysis_context, close_time, sl_pips, tp_pips
TradeOpenedPayload dataclass has fields: trade_id, pair, direction, entry_price, sl_pips, tp_pips, lots, confidence, regime, model
PolicyBlockedPayload dataclass has fields: action_type, decision, reasons, matched_rules, environment_snapshot
create_trade_closed_event(outcome_data: dict, session_id: str) -> TradingEvent factory function exists and generates a UUID event_id
validate_event(event: TradingEvent) -> bool function exists and checks required fields are non-empty
python -c 'from src.scanner.automation.trading_events import TradingEventType, TradingEvent, TradeClosedPayload, create_trade_closed_event, validate_event' succeeds
Syntax validation passes: python -m py_compile src/scanner/automation/trading_events.py
userStories.notes: Use @dataclass(frozen=True) for immutable events. Use uuid.uuid4().hex for event_id generation. Use datetime.utcnow().isoformat() for timestamps. Import patterns: from dataclasses import dataclass, field; from enum import Enum; import uuid. The payload_version field enables forward compatibility. All fields should have type hints.

userStories.title: Create trading_event_bus.py with blinker-based pub/sub
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a thread-safe trading event bus that supports priority-ordered handlers, idempotent processing, and JSONL history so that post-trade fan-out is reliable and inspectable.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at src/scanner/automation/trading_event_bus.py

TradingEventBus class exists with methods: subscribe(event_type, handler_fn, priority, handler_name), unsubscribe(handler_name), emit(event), emit_to_queue(event), get_history(event_type=None, limit=50)
subscribe() uses blinker.Signal per event_type for thread-safe dispatch
Idempotency uses cachetools.LRUCache(maxsize=10000) to track processed event_ids — emit() skips already-processed events
emit() calls handlers in priority order (lower number = higher priority)
History appends to trained_data/trading_events.jsonl using safe_jsonl_append from src.scanner.automation.safe_json
Logging uses structlog with bound context (event_type, event_id) on each emit
get_trading_event_bus() singleton function exists and returns same instance
reset_trading_event_bus() function exists for testing
python -c 'from src.scanner.automation.trading_event_bus import TradingEventBus, get_trading_event_bus' succeeds
Syntax validation passes: python -m py_compile src/scanner/automation/trading_event_bus.py
userStories.notes: Import blinker.Signal for per-event-type signals. Use cachetools.LRUCache for bounded idempotency set. Use structlog.get_logger() for structured logging. Import safe_jsonl_append from src.scanner.automation.safe_json for history persistence. The emit_to_queue() method should accept an optional queue parameter — for now it can just call emit() since the queue doesn't exist yet. Handlers should be sorted by priority before dispatch. Each handler call should be wrapped in try/except to isolate failures.

userStories.title: Unit tests for trading_event_bus.py
userStories.description: As a developer, I need tests for the event bus to verify thread safety, priority ordering, idempotency, and history persistence.
acceptanceCriteria: File created at tests/test_trading_event_bus.py

At least 8 tests covering: subscribe and emit delivers to handler, unsubscribe stops delivery, priority ordering (lower number fires first), idempotency (same event_id emitted twice only fires handler once), get_history returns emitted events, singleton get_trading_event_bus returns same instance, reset_trading_event_bus creates fresh instance, handler exception does not crash bus (other handlers still fire)
Tests pass: python -m pytest tests/test_trading_event_bus.py -v
userStories.notes: Use reset_trading_event_bus() in setUp/tearDown to isolate tests. For idempotency test: create event, emit twice, verify handler called exactly once. For priority test: subscribe handler_a at priority=10, handler_b at priority=5 — verify handler_b fires first. Use tmp_path fixture for JSONL history file. For exception isolation: subscribe a handler that raises, then another that doesn't — verify second handler still executes.
